topic: We already endure hardship, just for the wrong things: we stay up past midnight scrolling, wake tired after a night out, push through overwork without complaint, yet twenty minutes of training feels too hard; the capacity to endure is already there, the question is what we spend it on
figure: Musonius Rufus, Roman Stoic teacher of the 1st century AD and teacher of Epictetus (Lecture 7, That one should disdain hardships: people endure great toil for base ends, lovers for an illicit affair, others for profit or fame, and acrobats and athletes risk and suffer for small rewards; it would be absurd not to bear hardship willingly for something good). Paraphrased, not quoted. Single quote page, at Mintra's request
